name: S-Class Characters: The Agent Elite
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced.

The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

Agent Elite, S-Class

Hold on, we’re doing this again? Don’t get me wrong; I’m all for getting the last drop out of a bottle, but didn’t this stop being relevant in 2022? Wait, you’re telling me there was more in 2023? And we got a proper series finale!? And you’re offering me how much to narrate this with my sultry voice? Nothing? Oh, well, worth a shot. Excuse me a moment while I “prepare.” Glug Glug Okay, I’m ready.

Somehow, the totally awesome agent elite is now going to be even awesomer (it’s a word, I checked). Get ready to enjoy the greatest drinking game of all time. Oh, and feel free to invite your friends to join you (For legal reasons, we’re just going to assume you’re drinking Glen’s coolaid. Blue: For the best of times.)

Note: The s-class agent elite is an alternate version of the already superior agent elite class. They retain all of the standard agent elite progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select agent elite archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d10.

Parent Classes: Brawler and investigator.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.)

Class Skills

The s-class agent elite’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Climb (Str), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class agent elite.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

An s-class agent elite is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and firearms. They are proficient with light armor, but not with shields.

Genius Charm (Ex)

An s-class agent elite is both quick thinking and charismatic in deadly situations. At 1st level, he chooses Intelligence or Charisma. He can add that ability modifier to his melee attacks in place of Strength. Beginning at 3rd level, he also adds the chosen ability modifier to damage he deals with melee weapons in place of Strength.

Inspiration (Ex)

An s-class agent elite has the ability to augment skill checks and ability checks through his brilliant inspiration. The agent elite has an inspiration pool equal to 1/2 his agent elite level + his Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).

All of this goodness couldn’t even be contained in a single page. Serious props to Indi Martin for the best possible icon representing the agent elite.

* For this purpose, the GM and non-agents can also give you inspiration as well by joining in.

An s-class agent elite’s inspiration pool resets to 1 each day, typically after he gets a restful night’s sleep. As a free action, he can expend one use of inspiration from his pool to add 1d6 to the result of that check, including any on which he takes 10 or 20. This choice is made after the check is rolled and before the results are revealed. An s-class agent elite can only use inspiration once per check or roll. The agent can use inspiration on any Knowledge, Linguistics, or Spellcraft skill checks without expending a use of inspiration, provided he’s trained in the skill.

Inspiration can also be used on attack rolls and saving throws, at the cost of expending two uses of inspiration each time from the agent elite’s pool. In the case of saving throws, using inspiration is an immediate action rather than a free action.

Martial Training (Ex)

At 1st level, an s-class agent elite counts his total agent elite levels as both fighter levels and monk levels for the purpose of qualifying for feats. He also counts as both a fighter and a monk for feats and magic items that have different effects based on whether the character has levels in those classes (such as Stunning Fist and a monk’s robe). This ability does not automatically grant feats normally granted to fighters and monks based on class level, namely Stunning Fist.

Note: Monk’s robes can be worn normally, granting an s-class agent elite unarmed damage and the AC bonus of a 5th-level monk. Alternatively, an s-class agent elite wearing monk’s robes can treat his agent elite level as 5 higher when determining his drunken accuracy damage and liquid courage bonus. Once this choice is made, it cannot be changed for that particular magic item.

The Setup (Ex)

Since everybody’s going to play an agent elite* anyway (I mean, why wouldn’t you?), you can all grant 1 inspiration to somebody else at the table 1/minute if you take a drink of whatever you have available, to all appropriate maximums.

Seriously, though. You’d be crazy not to take at least one level in this class. Sorcerer or Wizard? Boom, you have decent melee thanks to genius charm. Literally any class where having a solid right hook helps? The agent has you covered. All I’m saying is, this is what the original summoner warns her kids about if they don’t go to sleep at night. Is it balanced? Always (I wouldn’t dare otherwise). Is it fair? Not even remotely.

IF you or your GM insist on having a little less up front, you can use the alternate unarmed damage boost starting with 1d4 and going up every 4 levels, but every time you roll better than average damage with an unarmed strike from 1st-level onward, you also need to take a drink of whatever you have available. If you don’t, you lose 1 inspiration point.

Agent Talents (Ex or Su)

At 2nd level and every 3 levels thereafter (5th, 8th, and so on), an s-class agent elite gains an agent talent. Except where otherwise noted, each agent talent can only be selected once.

A sample list of agent talents can be found at the end of this section.

Drink ‘Til You’re Good at It (Ex)

At 2nd level, when an s-class agent elite attempts any skill check, he can take a drink of alcohol as part of that action. If he does, he can replace his check result with a result of 10 + 1/2 his agent elite level + his Charisma modifier (inspiration spent on the attempt still applies). If he attempts this with a trained only skill in which he is untrained, the agent elite can only use the result above.

Hair of the Dog (Ex)

At 2nd level, an s-class agent elite gains a +2 bonus on his saving throw against poison (except alcohol) when you take a drink of whatever you have available right before you attempt it. This bonus increases to +4 at 5th level, and then again to +6 at 8th level. At 10th level, He becomes completely immune to poison.

Danger Zone!

At 3rd level, an s-class agent can select an investigator talent or one combat maneuver to receive additional training. He gains a +1 bonus on combat maneuver checks when performing that combat maneuver and a +1 bonus to his CMD when defending against that maneuver.

At 7th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the agent becomes further trained in another investigator talent or combat maneuver, gaining the above +1 bonus combat maneuver checks and to CMD. In addition, the bonuses granted by all previous maneuver training increase by 1 each.

Drunken Inspiration (Su)

At 3rd level, an s-class agent elite can drink a tankard of ale or strong alcohol and gain one temporary inspiration point. The act of drinking is a standard action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. The agent elite can have a maximum number of drunken inspiration points equal to 1 plus one additional point for every two levels thereafter (5th, 7th, and so on). These drunken inspiration points last for 1 hour or until spent, whichever is shorter. As long as he has at least 1 drunken inspiration point, the agent elite can spend 1 inspiration point as a swift action to move 5 feet without provoking attacks of opportunity.

Keen Recollection (Ex)

At 3rd level, an s-class agent elite can attempt all Knowledge skill checks untrained.

Knockout (Ex)

At 4th level, once per day an s-class agent elite can unleash a devastating attack that can instantly knock a target unconscious. He must announce this intent before making his attack roll. If the agent elite hits and the target takes damage from the blow, the target must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw (DC = 10 + 1/2 the agent elite’s level + his genius charm modifier) or fall unconscious for 1d6 rounds. Each round on its turn, the unconscious target may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect as a full-round action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures immune to critical hits or nonlethal damage are immune to this ability. At 10th level, the agent elite may use this ability twice per day; at 16th level, he may use it three times per day.

Liquid Courage (Ex)

At 4th level, an s-class agent elite gains a +3 morale bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects as long as he has at least 1 point of drunken inspiration. This bonus increases by +1 at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 20th level, to a maximum of +7.

Drunken Accuracy (Su)

At 5th level, an s-class agent elite can spend 1 point of inspiration as a swift action to inflict 1d6 extra points of damage on a single successful attack. The agent elite can choose to apply the damage after the attack roll is made.

At 10th level, the agent elite may instead spend 2 drunken inspiration points to increase the extra damage to 2d6. At 15th level, he may spend 3 drunken inspiration points to increase the extra damage to 3d6. At 20th level, he may spend 4 drunken inspiration points to increase the extra damage to 4d6. The agent elite must have at least 1 drunken inspiration point to use this ability.

Bonus Combat Feats

At 6th level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class agent elite gains a bonus combat feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. The agent elite must meet the prerequisites of the selected bonus combat feat. Upon reaching 9th level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class agent elite can choose to learn a new bonus combat feat in place of a bonus combat feat he has already learned. In effect, the agent elite loses the bonus combat feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. An s-class agent elite can only change one feat at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time he gains a new bonus combat feat for the level.

Drink ‘Til You’re Great at It (Ex)

At 7th level, an s-class agent elite chooses one skill. When he uses drink ‘til you’re good at it with that skill, the agent elite also benefits from its skill unlocks as if he possessed the Signature Skill feat and ranks equal to his agent elite level. He can choose a second such skill at 12th level, and a third at 17th level.

Drunken Courage (Su)

At 11th level, an s-class agent elite is immune to fear as long as he has at least 1 point of drunken inspiration.

Drunken Resilience (Ex)

At 13th level, an s-class agent elite gains DR 1/— as long as he has at least 1 point of drunken inspiration. At 16th level, the DR increases to 2/—. At 19th level, it increases to 3/—.

The Payoff (Ex)

Well, you did it hic, you got to 13th level. Now, when you threaten a critical hit with your unarmed strike, anybody else at the table can take a drink of whatever they have available to grant you a +1 bonus to your critical confirmation roll.

These bonuses stack between friends, but only +1 each (drink responsibly).

Drink ‘Til You’re the Best at It (Ex)

At 17th level, an s-class agent elite adds his full agent elite level to his result when using drink ‘til you’re good at it.

True Inspiration (Ex)

At 20th level, an s-class agent elite can use inspiration on all ability checks and skill checks without spending inspiration (even if he isn’t trained in a particular skill).

Whenever he does choose to expend inspiration on an ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, he adds 2d6 rather than 1d6 to the result. Some talents can affect this. If using the amazing inspiration investigator talent, he rolls 2d8 instead. If using this with empathy, tenacious inspiration, underworld inspiration, or a similar talent, he rolls two sets of inspiration dice and uses the higher of the two results. 4

Agent Talents
Combative (Ex)

Add Intimidate to your list of class skills. You also gain Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat. Beginning at 3rd level, you still add your Strength modifier to damage dealt with melee attacks in addition to your genius charm modifier.

As an s-class agent elite, choosing this agent talent more than once does nothing for you that you don’t already get while leveling up; so find something else.

Definitely a Clone (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 14th-level agent elite, probably not a clone agent talent.

If you are reduced to 0 or fewer hit points and you’re unable to successfully hide, you can choose for your body and all of your possessions to melt into a pool of acid that fills your space as a free action. At the beginning of your next turn, you can step out from anywhere into a space that can fit you comfortably. You have full hit points and equipment, but none of your limited-use abilities (including spell slots, if you have them).

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it or probably not a clone again for one week unless you take a drink of whatever you have available and pay enough gold for a scroll containing a breath of life spell (typically 1,125 gp, which also happens to be the going price to ship another disposable clone to your general location; not that that’s definitely what’s happening…).

Don’t Get Up (Ex)

When you are prone, you take no penalties to attacks you make, and creatures don’t gain bonuses to attack you.

You can flank while prone as long as you would meet the requirements if you were standing.

When you have remained at the table for at least 5 minutes without getting up, increase your weapon’s critical threat range by 1 until you get up. If you absolutely have to get up, anybody else at the table can take a drink of whatever they have available to maintain your bonus while you’re away.

Improved Staying Hydrated (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): Staying hydrated agent talent.

You can apply staying hydrated’s effects to damage dealt by you, an ally who can see and hear you, or an enemy who can see and hear you. This can’t force you or your ally to deal less overall damage, and it can’t allow an enemy to deal more overall damage.

Phrasing (Ex)

When another creature you can hear and that can hear you fails a Bluff, Diplomacy, or Intimidate check, you can spend an inspiration point and draw attention to it. This allows you to make your own check with the same skill to benefit yourself (your check can also benefit the creature you called out, but it must benefit you). If you fail this attempt by 4 or less, the attitude of the creature you called out is decreased by one step toward you. If you fail by 5 or more, the attitude of all creatures involved is decreased by one step toward you.

Probably Not a Clone (Su)

Once per day, if you are reduced to 0 or fewer hit points and you’re one move action away from being able to hide, you can take a drink of whatever you have available to move up to your speed and make a Stealth check to hide as an immediate action. If your check is successful against every creature present (including your allies, but they can conveniently just choose not to see you), you begin the next round by stepping back into view as a free action with hit points equal to half your total, since suddenly being totally undamaged could draw too much attention.

Say it Again (Ex)

As a full-round action, you can spend any combination of 3 inspiration or drunken inspiration points to gain a hero point. Whenever somebody at the table repeats a common phrase in your group, you can take a drink of whatever you have available to gain a hero point, to a maximum of 3 hero points. This doesn’t function if they’re only saying it to benefit from this agent talent.

Staying Hydrated (Ex)

If whatever you have available to you is a standard, nonalcoholic beverage (preferably water, but no need to be picky), good for you. Once per round, you can take a drink of it as a free action and reroll one attack roll, skill check, saving throw, or ability check. Otherwise (or if you have two or more drinks handy, choose one for each), you can take a drink of whatever you have available whenever you need an opponent who can see and hear you to reroll one attack roll, skill check, saving throw, or ability check.

You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier.

Take One For the Team (Ex)

Once per day, if any of your allies within one move of you would be reduced to 0 or fewer hit points and can’t (or fail to) use probably not a clone, you can take a drink of whatever you have available as an immediate action to move to that ally, shove them to a safe, adjacent, unoccupied space, and take their place.

You can select this agent talent more than once, which allows you to use it on additional allies, but not more than once per day on a single ally.

What Fourth Wall? (Ex)

Whenever an agent elite class feature calls for you to drink a tankard of ale or strong alcohol and you don’t have any, you can instead take a drink of whatever you have available to gain those benefits.

Sample Investigator Talents

This sample list of talents is intentionally summarized for easy reference. Please see individual sources for additional information and talents.

Amazing Inspiration

Prerequisite(s): 7th level.

Benefit(s): Your inspiration die is a d8. At 20th level, you roll 2d8 for inspiration instead.

Combat Inspiration

Prerequisite(s): 9th level.

Benefit(s): It costs you 1 inspiration to add inspiration on attack rolls and saving throws.

Combat Inspiration, Greater

Prerequisite(s): 19th level, combat inspiration.

Benefit(s): Choose one specific weapon type (such as short swords or longbows). It costs you no inspiration to add inspiration on attack rolls and saving throws with the chosen weapons as long as you have at least 1 inspiration remaining in your pool.

Effortless Aid

Benefit(s): You can use an aid another action as a move action instead of as a standard action, and you can spend 1 inspiration to instead perform an aid another action as a swift action.

Eidetic Recollection

Prerequisite(s): 11th level.

Benefit(s): You can always choose to take 10 on any Knowledge check, even if you’re in immediate danger or distracted. You can also spend 1 inspiration to take 20 on a Knowledge skill check even if you’re in immediate danger or distracted.

Expanded Inspiration

Benefit(s): You can use inspiration on Diplomacy, Heal, Perception, Profession, and Sense Motivechecks without spending inspiration, provided you’re trained in that skill.

Inspirational Expertise

Prerequisite(s): 7th level.

Benefit(s): When you successfully identify a creature with monster lore using a Knowledge skill, you can spend 1 inspiration as a swift action and grant allies within 30 feet that can hear you a +4 insight bonus on attack rolls against creatures of that type for 1 round.

Inspired Alertness

Benefit(s): When you would become flat-footed, you can spend 1 inspiration using no action to ignore it.

Inspired Intimidator

Benefit(s): When you successfully demoralize a creature with Intimidate, you can spend inspiration as part of that action to increase the duration by 1 round per point of inspiration spent in this way.

Perceptive Tracking

Benefit(s): You can use Perception in place of Survival to find both find and follow tracks, using the same DCs listed under the Survival skill.

Advanced Weapon Training (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Fighter level 5th, weapon training class feature.

Benefit(s): Select one advanced weapon training option, applying it to one fighter weapon group you have already selected with the weapon training class feature.

Special: This feat can be taken more than once, but at most once per 5 fighter levels.

All-Consuming Swing (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Str 13, Power Attack, Cleave, Vital Strike, base attack bonus +8.

Benefit(s): You can use Cleave and Vital Strike together, but you also take the additional damage dealt by Vital Strike.

Blind-Fight (Combat)

Benefit(s): You can reroll melee miss chance versus concealment (but not blink) once per round. Creatures in melee with you gain no benefits to their attacks for being invisible.

Bodyguard (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Combat Reflexes.

Benefit(s): When an adjacent ally is attacked, you may use an attack of opportunity to attempt the aid another action to improve your ally’s AC. You may not use the aid another action to improve your ally’s attack roll with this attack.

Cleave (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Str 13, Power Attack, base attack bonus +1.

Benefit(s): As a standard action, you can take a –2 penalty to your AC until the start of your next turn and make a single attack roll. If your attack hits and there’s another creature within reach, you can attack that creature with the same attack bonus.

Combat Expertise (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Int 13.

Benefit(s): Before you attack or use a combat maneuver, you can choose to take a –1 penalty on all associated rolls this round and gain a +1 dodge bonus to your AC. At 4th-level and every 4 levels thereafter, you can take an additional –1 penalty and increase your AC accordingly.

Combat Reflexes (Combat)

Benefit(s): You may make a number of additional attacks of opportunity per round equal to your Dexterity bonus. With this feat, you may also make attacks of opportunity while flat-footed.

Critical Focus (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Base attack bonus +9.

Benefit(s): You receive a +4 circumstance bonus on attack rolls made to confirm critical hits.

Disruptive (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): 6th-level fighter.

Benefit(s): The DC to cast spells defensively increases by +4 for all enemies that are within your threatened area. This increase to casting spells defensively only applies if you are aware of the enemy’s location and are capable of taking an attack of opportunity.

If you can only take one attack of opportunity per round and have already used that attack, this increase does not apply.

Great Cleave (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Str 13, Cleave Power Attack, base attack bonus +4.

Benefit(s): When you use Cleave, you can keep attacking new targets within reach while you continue to hit.

Greater Feint (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Int 13, Combat Expertise, Improved Feint, base attack bonus +6.

Benefit(s): Whenever you use feint to cause an opponent to lose his Dexterity bonus, he loses that bonus until the beginning of your next turn, in addition to losing his Dexterity bonus against your next attack.

Greater Weapon Focus (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Weapon Focus, fighter level 8th.

Benefit(s): Your Weapon Focus bonus becomes +2.

Greater Weapon Specialization (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Greater Weapon Focus, fighter level 12th.

Benefit(s): Your Weapon Specialization bonus becomes +4.

Improved Feint (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Int 13, Combat Expertise.

Benefit(s): You can make a Bluff check to feint in combat as a move action.

Improved Initiative (Combat)

Benefit(s): You get a +4 bonus on initiative checks.

Power Attack (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Str 13, base attack bonus +1.

Benefit(s): Before you attack, you can choose to take a –1 penalty on all attack rolls this round and gain a +2 bonus to your weapon’s damage (+1 if off-hand or light, +3 if twohanded). At 4th-level and every 4 levels thereafter, you can take an additional –1 penalty and increase your damage accordingly.

Vital Strike (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Base attack bonus +6.

Benefit(s): When you use the attack action, you can make a single attack. If you hit, double your weapon’s damage dice. These additional dice are not multiplied on a critical hit.

Special: You can select this feat again at base attack bonus +11 and +16. At +11, triple your weapon’s damage dice, and at +16, quadruple them.

Weapon Focus (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Base attack bonus +1, proficiency with the weapon.

Benefit(s): You gain a +1 bonus on attack rolls with a specific weapon.

Weapon Specialization (Combat)

Prerequisite(s): Weapon Focus, fighter level 4th, proficiency with the weapon.

Benefit(s): You gain a +2 bonus on damage rolls with a specific weapon.
